title: Drive analytics writes one counter per operation with four dimension paths, so a question like which files were moved last week is a dimension filter rather than a scan
content:
The `drive-analytics` package ships two processors — `DriveAnalyticsProcessor` for document-drive operations and `DocumentAnalyticsProcessor` for individual document operations — both converting operations into time-series points with dimensions.

The primary metric is deliberately trivial: **`DriveOperations`, a counter whose value is 1 for each operation**, at per-operation timestamp precision. All the analytical power sits in four dimension paths:

| Dimension | Path format | Example |
| --- | --- | --- |
| Drive | `ph/drive/{driveId}/{branch}/{scope}/{revision}` | `ph/drive/abc123/main/global/42` |
| Operation | `ph/drive/operation/{operationType}/{operationIndex}` | `ph/drive/operation/ADD_FILE/5` |
| Target | `ph/drive/target/{targetType}/{targetId}` — `DRIVE` or `NODE` | `ph/drive/target/NODE/file123` |
| Action type | `ph/drive/actionType/{actionType}/{targetId}` | `ph/drive/actionType/CREATED/file123` |

The **action-type dimension is the interpretive one**, folding raw operations into five verbs: `CREATED` (`ADD_FILE`, `ADD_FOLDER`), `DUPLICATED` (`COPY_NODE`), `UPDATED` (`UPDATE_FILE`, `UPDATE_NODE`), `MOVED` (`MOVE_NODE`), `REMOVED` (`DELETE_NODE`). That is what lets a dashboard ask "how much creation happened" without enumerating operation names.

Two operational behaviours: operations are processed in **configurable chunks (default 50)**, and the processor **clears and rebuilds analytics data when processing from index 0** — so a replay from the start is idempotent rather than doubling every count. Analytics data is organised under the source path `ph/drive/{documentId}/{branch}/{scope}`.
